sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 7:5

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 7:5:1
items.html:
The root of ZA is but six Sefirot: For when it is born it lacks a Rosh [head], which is the GAR [first three] called HBD, and it then has only VAK [six ends], which are HGT NHY alone. And Malchut has nothing but her own Malchut, and she lacks all the first nine Sefirot. Therefore the Sitra Achra has no nursing whatsoever from the Rosh of ZA, since at the time of Katnut [smallness] it has no Rosh.
There is a great matter in these words, as will be explained further on, God willing, and here we shall explain only the reason for the thing: why ZA emerged lacking GAR. And in truth, even at the time of Gadlut [greatness] it has no more than six vessels, HGT NHY. And what the ARI writes, that it then has ten Sefirot, does not mean that the first three Sefirot, which are KHB, were added to it, but only that its HGT of Katnut grow and become HBD for it, and the NHY of Katnut grow and become HGT for it, and only the three lower Sefirot, which are NHY, were added to it. Thus even at the time of Gadlut it does not attain the first three vessels, KHB. And since this is a great principle in the wisdom, we must understand it from its source, each thing with its reason.
And it is known that the root of ZA emerged in the Nekudim, which is called the HaVaYaH of BON, which is the Partzuf MA called YESHSUT that emerged from the Nikvey Einayim. And you find in this Partzuf a great innovation, differing from all the preceding Partzufim of AK; for in them the Gufim emerged with ten Sefirot and ten vessels, and every Guf [body] begins from the vessel of Keter, as written concerning Mati [reaching] and Lo Mati [not reaching]; see there. But in this Partzuf, which emerged from the Einayim, the Guf begins from Daat, and there is in them no trace of the first three Sefirot, Keter, Hochma and Bina. Besides this, there is a great change in the ten Sefirot of the Rosh itself, for until here every Partzuf has only one Rosh, whereas in the Partzuf of the Einayim the Partzuf has three Roshim: the first is YESHSUT, which stands from the Tabur of AK upward as far as the Chazeh [chest]; the second is the Keter of Nekudim; the third is AVI of Nekudim.
Indeed these two changes depend upon one another, for it has already been well explained in Part 6 that all these three Roshim are but the ten Sefirot of a single Rosh. And the matter of their dividing thus is because of the ascent of the bottom Hey to the Einayim, so that the coupling was made upon the screen of phase one, which is called Nikvey Einayim. And the first Rosh emerged with two Sefirot, Keter and Hochma, and in the Nukva of Hochma the coupling was made upon the bottom Hey included there, and this Rosh is called YESHSUT. Therefore the three Sefirot Bina, ZA and Malchut are regarded as the HGT of the Rosh, for since they are found below the screen and below the place of the coupling, they thereby left the category of GAR.
And even so, these HGT too are regarded as a Rosh; moreover, they are the essential Rosh of the Partzuf of Nekudim. For the aforementioned first Rosh, called YESHSUT, which stands from the Tabur of AK upward as far as the Chazeh, is not joined at all to the Partzuf of Nekudim, but is counted entirely as Akudim, as written there. (See Inner Light, page 409, the passage beginning “GAR.”) Only its AHP, which went outside into HGT, are counted as the Rosh of Nekudim.
Indeed these AHP too divide into two Roshim, for the Ozen [ear], which is called the Sefira of Keter of Nekudim, is counted as the Keter and Hochma of this Rosh, in the secret of the bottom Hey in the Einayim; and the Hotem [nose] and Peh [mouth], which went outside from this Rosh as well, in the secret of YHV in the AHP, are counted as the third Rosh, called AVI of Nekudim. And know that the second Rosh too, called the Keter of Nekudim, is likewise not counted as the Rosh of the Partzuf — that is, its Malchut does not expand from above downward into the ten Sefirot of the Guf, for it illuminates and clothes in the third Rosh alone, namely in AVI of Nekudim. And only AVI of Nekudim are the Rosh of the Partzuf of Nekudim, that is, their Malchut expands from above downward into the ten Sefirot of the Guf of Nekudim. (As written in the Inner Observation above, page 459, item 30; study it there well, the whole continuation.) And know that even at the time of Gadlut, when the bottom Hey descends from the Einayim in Keter to the Peh of the Rosh, and AVI return to being a Rosh, still the Keter itself does not join AVI in such a way that they become literally one Rosh, but only the illumination of the NHY of Keter clothes in AVI. And this is the secret of AVI becoming HBD, while the second Rosh is Keter above their Rosh.
And you see how the ten Sefirot of a single Rosh divided and became three Roshim: the Keter and Hochma among them were taken by the first Rosh; the Bina among them, which is called Ozen, was taken by the second Rosh; and the ZAT among them, which are called Hotem and Peh, were taken by the third Rosh, called AVI, who are counted as the Rosh of this Partzuf. But the two preceding Roshim are not joined to the Guf of the Partzuf, as above.
And you already know that all the Sefirot of the Guf are drawn from the Rosh, for whatever measure the Malchut of the Rosh clothes with her reflected light from below upward in the Rosh, that same quantity she expands, from herself and within herself, into the ten Sefirot of the Guf. With this you will understand that the Malchut of the third Rosh could expand into the Guf only in the seven lower Sefirot, HGT NHYM alone, since in the Rosh too she has no more than the two Sefirot Hotem and Peh, which are the ZAT of the Rosh. And the GAR of the Rosh are found in the two preceding Roshim, for Keter and Hochma are found in the first Rosh, called YESHSUT, and Bina is found in the second Rosh, called Keter, as above. And now it is well explained that it is impossible for ZON to have more than seven vessels, HGT NHYM, because their Rosh too, which is AVI, has no more than these ZAT, which are Hotem and Peh.
And one should raise no difficulty from this — if so, wherein lies the superiority of AVI over ZON, since both of them lack GAR? For the ARI has already explained this matter to us above (from page 411 to 415, from item 21 to item 25): that the whole praise of AVI over ZON is because AVI took a little illumination from the light of the Ozen, and therefore their vessels were not broken; and only ZON, who received no illumination whatsoever from the light of the Ozen but from the Hotem and Peh alone, therefore all their vessels were broken. Study it there well, and in the Inner Light. In general it has already been well explained there, and it will be further explained before us in this part, that this illumination which AVI received from the light of the Ozen corrected them in the secret of the coupling back to back, which is the secret that through this they had the GAR of Bina, as will be written further on at length.
